heading: INT. ORBITAL GREENHOUSE RING - "SOLARIUM 3" - NIGHT CYCLE

units.text: INT. ORBITAL GREENHOUSE RING - "SOLARIUM 3" - NIGHT CYCLE
A curved corridor of glass and ribbed steel, wrapped around a slow-turning station.
Rows of tomato vines climb silver trellises under violet grow-lamps.
Beyond the glass, Saturn's rings burn thin and gold against black.
DR. IMOGEN FAIRWEATHER-OKORO (50s, close-cropped gray hair, a patched blue jumpsuit, hands stained green to the wrist) walks the rows with a tablet.
She is humming.
She stops at a vine and presses a ripe tomato between thumb and finger.
Good girl.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: She plucks it, bites in, closes her eyes.
The station is quiet.
The lamps hum on a calm note.
Everything is exactly as it should be.
She taps the tablet and speaks into it.
Greenhouse log, day four hundred and twelve. Yield nominal. Humidity nominal. Crew morale...
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: She smiles at the empty corridor.
Nominal. Seeing as I'm the crew.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: A soft chime.
The tablet screen flickers.
A recorded voice, her own, younger, bright, comes through the speaker.
Log, day one. If you're hearing this, Imogen, then the relief ship is overdue and I've been right about the schedule all along.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: Imogen's smile fades.
She lifts the tablet and scrolls.
A file she does not remember is open.
Don't go to the east vines. The ones in the corner. Don't water them. Don't touch them. They aren't ours.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: Imogen turns her head slowly.
At the end of the ring, past the last trellis, a single vine she has never planted is climbing the glass, pulsing, in time with her breath.
